name: claim_enrichment_table_record
description:
Checks and marks a key in a `memory` enrichment table in one step, so a burst of events
with the same key counts every event even before the table publishes its writes to
readers.

The first claim on a key with no live row opens a window of `window_secs`, which stays
fixed from then on. Each claim in the window counts; the first `cap` of them pass.
The returned object has `pass`, `first` (this claim opened the window), `count` (this
claim's position in the window, from 1), `suppressed_prev` (on the claim that opens a
window, how many the previous window suppressed while its row was still live),
`window_secs` (the window in force) and `value` (what the opening claim stored).

The row is written through the table's own write path, so its size cap, TTL scan and
persistence apply to it.

arguments.name: table
arguments.description: The [enrichment table](/docs/reference/glossary/#enrichment-tables) to claim the key in. Only `memory` tables support claims.

arguments.name: key
arguments.description: The key to check and mark.

arguments.name: window_secs
arguments.description: The length of the window this claim opens when the key has no live row, in seconds. At least 1. A window already open keeps its own length.

arguments.name: cap
arguments.description: How many claims in one window pass. At least 1.

arguments.name: ttl_secs
arguments.description: How long the row lives from the start of the window this claim opens, in seconds. At least `window_secs`, which is the default. A longer row lets the claim that opens the next window report how many the previous window suppressed.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: A value stored by the claim that opens the window and returned to every claim in it.

internal_failure_reasons: The table does not support claims.

examples.title: Throttle a key to one event a minute
